title: The natural world
subtitle: whiskers, petals, blossom, breed
summary: Name the parts of animals and plants, learn some less familiar creatures, and use the verbs that describe what happens in nature.

lesson.heading: Parts of birds and animals
rows: the part a bird uses to fly
one of the light soft things that cover a bird's body
the place a bird builds to lay its eggs in
the soft thick hair on an animal such as a cat or a fox
the long stiff hairs that stick out from a cat's face
the sharp curved nails on an animal's or bird's foot
the foot of an animal such as a cat or a dog
the part at the back end of an animal's body
the long hair on the neck of a lion or a horse
the hard pointed growths on the head of a cow or a goat

lesson.heading: Parts of a flower
rows: the coloured outer parts of a flower
the fine yellow powder bees carry from flower to flower
a flower that is closed and just about to open
the long thin part that holds up the flower
a sharp point on the stem of a plant such as a rose
a flat green part of a plant (plural: leaves)

lesson.heading: Parts of a tree
rows: the thick main stem of a tree
the rough outer covering of a tree's trunk
an arm of a tree growing out from the trunk
the parts that grow under the ground
lesson.note: Two very common trees are the *oak* and the *willow*.

lesson.heading: Creatures you may not know
rows: worm, snail, deer (singular and plural), fox, bat
lesson.note: A bat is not a bird - it is a mammal, and it uses a kind of radar to find its way around.

lesson.heading: Verbs for processes in nature
lesson.text: These verbs and their objects go together so regularly that it is worth learning them as pairs.

examples.text: These birds **lay their eggs** on the ground.
examples.note: lay, laid, laid - the bird laid three eggs

examples.text: Bees **collect pollen** from flowers to make honey.

right.label: Transitive - with an object
examples: We **grew some tomatoes** in our garden last year.
My neighbour **breeds Burmese cats** and sells them.

lesson.text: We **pick** flowers and fruit, never ~~pick up~~: *We picked some flowers and put them in a vase.* You **pick something up** only when it has fallen or been dropped.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with the part of the animal it names.

pairs.right: the hairs that stick out from a cat's face
the long hair on a lion's neck
the place where a bird lays its eggs
the foot of a cat or a dog

exercises.prompt: Bees help to move ___ from one flower to another as they collect nectar to make honey.
The part of a flower that usually has the brightest colours is the ___.
exercises.explanation: Petals are the coloured outer parts of a flower.

exercises.prompt: Is each word an animal word or a plant word?
A cat can sharpen its claws against the ___ of a tree.
exercises.explanation: Bark is the rough outer layer of a tree trunk.
A tree blossoms or flowers when its flowers come out.

exercises.prompt: Flowers last longer in a vase if you crush the end of their ___.
exercises.explanation: The stem is the long thin part that holds up the flower.

exercises.prompt: Take care not to prick yourself. That plant has sharp ___.
exercises.explanation: Thorns are the sharp points on the stem of a plant such as a rose.

exercises.prompt: ___ move very, very slowly and carry their shells with them.
exercises.explanation: A worm moves slowly too, but the snail is the classic slow mover.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings with the endings.

pairs.right: from the tree during the storm
some apples that had dropped from the tree
a new type of tomato that was very big
into the stream and swam away
some herbs to put on our pizza

options: The bird has lay three eggs.
exercises.explanation: *Lay, laid, laid* takes an object: the bird laid three eggs.

exercises.prompt: Which is the odd one out: a seal, a whale or a crab?
options: a crab - it has a shell and is a shellfish
a seal - it can come out of the water
a whale - it is the biggest
None of them; they are all the same kind of creature
exercises.explanation: Seals and whales are mammals; a crab is a shellfish.

exercises.statement: We picked up some flowers and put them in a vase.
exercises.explanation: We pick flowers and fruit: We picked some flowers and put them in a vase. You pick something up only when it has fallen.
